narrative:
The model estimates a 67% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors that stood out compared to employees the system expected to stay.

The strongest influence came from the fact that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal the model associates with higher turnover risk, pushing your prediction strongly toward leaving. 

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years worked in the opposite direction. Most employees the model predicted would stay also had limited experience, so this factor helped pull the prediction slightly back toward staying. However, it was not enough to outweigh the other signals.

The third important factor was your employment in the “other” sector. This category shows noticeably higher predicted leaving rates than the medical or education sectors that dominate the stay group, giving another moderate push toward the leave prediction.

Taken together, these elements led the system to conclude you are more likely to depart than to remain. The organization should discuss your career goals and any external offers openly with you. You might consider what would make staying more attractive, such as clearer advancement paths or addressing any concerns around sector-specific challenges. Understanding these drivers can help both sides find a positive way forward.
